strongest_objection: The type's 'no enforcer' clause is not the criterion the author applied, and the record contradicts itself on it. The of-sentence admits only parties with 'no shared history and no enforcer', and the boundary case throws out 'a court-enforced contract for the plainer reason that an enforcer exists'; yet the earn-out (Wager that needs a partner), source escrow and the posted bond (Hostage before the ask), the sharecrop, contingency fee and royalty (Price after the crop), and the irrevocable license (Rule against myself) are all court-enforced contracts, and the fair had its own court. The letter of credit was rejected in the ledger for a different reason entirely, that the parties never cooperate with each other. The criterion actually applied, and the one that makes the map good, is that the first move must survive without resting on the other party's word: a court in the background may make the payout collectable, but nothing in the mechanism asks either stranger to be trusted. The repair is to the type, not to the items. Replacement of-sentence: 'A mechanism by which two parties with no shared history make a first cooperative move that the bare payoffs would forbid and that rests on neither party's word, whether or not a court stands behind the paper, named with its carrier, what makes the first move survivable, who can strike it (one side alone, both hands at once, a third with a stake, or nobody), and the residue it leaves that later limits the cooperation.' Under that sentence the letter of credit stays out for the ledger's stated reason, the court-enforced contract stays out only when the contract itself is what makes the move safe, and the fourth boundary claim can stop apologizing for a gradient. Beyond the type I could not break the map: the strange members (a planted twenty, a shore with no faces, a sin as first act, a promise free until the barn burns, a tailor's cut) survive the neighbor and boundary tests below, and the itinerary's hinge teaches. What remains are illustrative cases that do not carry their own item's mechanism (source escrow is held by a third and grants use on release; the darknet escrow has a broker; a deductible is not a bet; co-founders chose each other), one misattribution, one false exclusivity claim on the fork, and one edge that calls a staged circumstance a probe when it is a manipulation that merely shares the probe's residue.

items.item: Twenty in the till: one party stages a windfall the other could keep without being caught, as a bar owner leaves a loose twenty in the drawer on a new bartender's first shift or a jeweler overpays a courier by one stone; the carrier is an apparent error, the first move is safe because the stake is small and its return is uncoerced information, and the residue is that the probe must stay secret forever, since a cooperation later found to have begun as a test reads as contempt; not a gift, which announces itself and makes a debt rather than a reading.
items.why: Tested against Lot you can lose (below) and it separates: the counterpart does not know a lot was extended, so what comes back is unperformed conduct. One modality softening belongs in the record rather than the item: in trades where the probe is customary (retail integrity shops, the counted-short float), discovery reads as routine and the secret residue shrinks toward zero, which limits how far the Enemy at both doors passage reaches.

items.item: Gift already eaten: one party delivers something the other has consumed before it could decide whether to accept, as a produce broker drops a case of stone fruit at a restaurant's back door on a Friday or the drug company's lunch is on the table before the clinic is asked; the carrier is a good whose acceptance is performed by its arrival, the first move is safe because it is sized to what the giver can lose, and the residue is a debt in an unpriced currency that the giver may name later and the receiver can never fully close; adjacent to cooperation-mechanisms' recursive gift exchange, which is the running loop, this is the unrefusable first turn, and its power is that no price was said.
items.why: Its residue, a debt in an unpriced currency the giver may name later, is word for word cooperative-masks' 'favor unasked-for, priced later', and the brief requires an adjacent item to say what it adds. The item cites only cooperation-mechanisms' gift loop. What it adds is real: the mask is this ignition used as a trap, while the ignition works whether or not the giver ever names the price.
items.repair: Gift already eaten: one party delivers something the other has consumed before it could decide whether to accept, as a produce broker drops a case of stone fruit at a restaurant's back door on a Friday or the drug company's lunch is on the table before the clinic is asked; the carrier is a good whose acceptance is performed by its arrival, the first move is safe because it is sized to what the giver can lose, and the residue is a debt in an unpriced currency that the giver may name later and the receiver can never fully close; adjacent to cooperation-mechanisms' recursive gift exchange, which is the running loop, and to cooperative-masks' favor unasked-for and priced later, which is this ignition used as a trap, this is the unrefusable first turn, which ignites whether or not the giver ever means to name the price, and its power is that no price was said.

items.item: Hostage before the ask: one party hands over, unrequested, something the other can destroy but not use, as a software vendor deposits its source in escrow before the customer thought to require it or a contractor posts a bond nobody demanded; the carrier is Schelling's asymmetry, precious to the giver and worthless to the holder, the first move is safe because it costs nothing if the other cooperates and says what words cannot, and the residue is that the holder keeps a permanent option to destroy and the cooperation cannot grow past the hostage's value without a second hostage; not collateral demanded, which is a term, and not cooperation-mechanisms' retained hostages, which steady a cooperation already running; here the unasked giving is the whole signal.
items.why: Neither illustrative case carries the item's own mechanism. Source in escrow is held by an escrow agent, not the counterpart, so the customer has no option to destroy, and on release the customer gains full use of the source, so the thing is not 'worthless to the holder'; the bond is money to a surety that the owner can claim and spend. Both are collateral with a third holder, which the item's own discriminator excludes. The asymmetry named, precious to the giver and worth little to the holder, is Williamson's ugly-princess condition from 'Credible Commitments' (1983), not Schelling's; Schelling's hostages are commitment devices in general. Replaced the cases with ones where the counterpart itself holds a thing it can only destroy, and named the asymmetry correctly.
items.repair: Hostage before the ask: one party hands over, unrequested, something the other can destroy but not use, as a demolition subcontractor parks its excavator on the owner's lot the night before any contract is signed, or a touring band leaves its backline in the club's cellar before the settlement is agreed; the carrier is the hostage asymmetry Williamson called the ugly princess, precious to the giver and worth little to the holder, so that holding it tempts no one to provoke a default, the first move is safe because it costs nothing if the other cooperates and says what words cannot, and the residue is that the holder keeps a permanent option to destroy and the cooperation cannot grow past the hostage's value without a second hostage; not collateral demanded, which is a term, not source escrow or a bond, where a third party holds the thing and the counterpart gains its use on release, and not cooperation-mechanisms' retained hostages, which steady a cooperation already running; here the unasked giving is the whole signal.

items.item: Beach with no faces: the exchange is arranged so that no step requires trusting the next, as in the reported silent trade where traders laid goods on the shore and withdrew, the other side laid gold beside them and withdrew, and the first party took the gold or left it if the pile was short; the carrier is a spatial protocol in which every move is retractable until the last, the first move is safe because at no moment does either party hold both goods, and the residue is that no channel exists, so the parties cannot complain, explain, bundle, or extend credit, and the cooperation cannot grow past spot exchange; Herodotus's account is disputed as history and is kept for the mechanism, which the two-key drop and the escrowed darknet sale reproduce.
items.why: The mechanism is sound and the Herodotus modality is honest, but the two modern reproductions are wrong. 'The two-key drop' names nothing an operator can find, and the escrowed darknet sale has a market holding the money, which is a broker with a face and exactly what the item claims to abolish. The atomic swap reproduces the silent trade precisely: each transfer is locked until the other's is revealed and either side can walk until the last step. The boundary case below also shows the residue (no channel) comes from the missing faces and not from the retractable protocol, so the discriminator now says so.
items.repair: Beach with no faces: the exchange is arranged so that no step requires trusting the next, as in the reported silent trade where traders laid goods on the shore and withdrew, the other side laid gold beside them and withdrew, and the first party took the gold or left it if the pile was short; the carrier is a spatial protocol in which every move is retractable until the last, the first move is safe because at no moment does either party hold both goods, and the residue is that no channel exists, so the parties cannot complain, explain, bundle, or extend credit, and the cooperation cannot grow past spot exchange; Herodotus's account is disputed as history and is kept for the mechanism, which the atomic swap reproduces exactly, each side's transfer locked until the other's is revealed and either side free to walk until the last step; the escrowed darknet sale does not, since its market is a holder with a face, and a cash sale across a counter has the protocol without the residue, since the faces leave a channel and the beach's ceiling is bought by their absence, not by the protocol.

items.item: Wager that needs a partner: two parties who disagree about a fact write the disagreement as a contingent term each thinks favors it, as buyer and seller who cannot agree on a company's worth sign an earn-out, an insurer and a shipowner who disagree about a hull split the risk by a deductible, two rivals bet on whose method yields more and must run the trial together; the carrier is a difference of belief, the first move is safe because each party expects to win, so the disagreement itself funds the cooperation, and the residue is that whoever measures wins, so the accounting or the trial design becomes the next fight; not impasse-inventions' invented chip, which breaks a deadlock in a negotiation already running, since here there was no relationship and the disagreement is the fuel.
items.why: The second case does not instantiate the mechanism: a hull deductible is a moral-hazard and small-claims device, not a contingent term two parties write because they disagree about a fact and each expects to win. The earn-out and the joint trial carry the item; replaced the deductible with percentage rent, which a landlord and tenant write exactly when they disagree about what a corner will draw. Also named the closer neighbor, impasse-inventions' graduated tie, since 'invented chip' alone does not tell the reader which one.
items.repair: Wager that needs a partner: two parties who disagree about a fact write the disagreement as a contingent term each thinks favors it, as buyer and seller who cannot agree on a company's worth sign an earn-out, a landlord and a tenant who disagree about the traffic a corner will draw set the rent as a share of sales, two rivals bet on whose method yields more and must run the trial together; the carrier is a difference of belief, the first move is safe because each party expects to win, so the disagreement itself funds the cooperation, and the residue is that whoever measures wins, so the accounting or the trial design becomes the next fight; not impasse-inventions' graduated tie or contingent clause, which break a deadlock in a negotiation already running, since here there was no relationship and the disagreement is the fuel.

items.item: Promise that costs nothing yet: each party promises to pay in a state that has not occurred, as farmers in a county pledge to cover any barn that burns or shipowners pledge to share any hull lost; the carrier is a contingency improbable enough that the promise is nearly free to make, the first move is safe because nothing is paid until the loss and every other promiser is still exposed when it comes, and the residue is that the cooperation is untested until the first claim, which is the real ignition and arrives when the promiser is poorest and least willing; not price after the crop, where the trigger is certain and only its size is unknown.
items.why: The residue claims the first claim 'arrives when the promiser is poorest', which is true only for a common shock (a storm that takes several hulls). For the barn mutual the promiser's barn is standing; what makes the first claim the real ignition is that paying now buys the payer nothing, since the claimant's good conduct is already spent. That is the sharper mechanism and it is the one the item wants. The item also sits directly on cooperation-mechanisms' 'mutualization of risk through insurance pools' without saying what it adds, which the brief requires.
items.repair: Promise that costs nothing yet: each party promises to pay in a state that has not occurred, as farmers in a county pledge to cover any barn that burns or shipowners pledge to share any hull lost; the carrier is a contingency improbable enough that the promise is nearly free to make, the first move is safe because nothing is paid until the loss and every other promiser is still exposed when it comes, and the residue is that the cooperation is untested until the first claim, which is the real ignition and arrives at the moment paying buys the payer nothing, since the claimant's good conduct is already spent and the payer's own barn still stands, and, when the shock is common and takes several hulls at once, arrives as well when the payer is poorest; not price after the crop, where the trigger is certain and only its size is unknown, and not cooperation-mechanisms' mutualization of risk, which is the pool running, since here the promise is the ignition and the first claim is its test.

items.item: Broker of both names: a third party with history on each side and no stake in the deal beyond its next introduction lends both its name, as a freight broker matches a shipper and a carrier who have never met, a literary agent puts a manuscript in an editor's hands, a Maghribi merchant vouched for an agent overseas; the carrier is a reputation held in the middle, the first move is safe because the broker loses its next match if either side cheats, and the residue is that the parties never build direct trust, the broker sees everything and takes a cut forever, and the first direct deal is the first betrayal; not an enforcer, since the broker can only withhold the next match, and not the bank's letter of credit, where nobody trusts anyone and each party transacts with the bank.
items.why: The item contradicts itself: the broker has 'no stake in the deal beyond its next introduction' and then 'takes a cut forever'. Freight brokers margin the load and agents take fifteen percent; the cut is the stake, and the mechanism needs it, since the broker's exposure is the future stream of cuts it loses if either side cheats. One phrase fixes it.
items.repair: Broker of both names: a third party with history on each side and no stake in the deal beyond its cut and its next introduction lends both its name, as a freight broker matches a shipper and a carrier who have never met, a literary agent puts a manuscript in an editor's hands, a Maghribi merchant vouched for an agent overseas; the carrier is a reputation held in the middle, the first move is safe because the broker loses its next match if either side cheats, and the residue is that the parties never build direct trust, the broker sees everything and takes a cut forever, and the first direct deal is the first betrayal; not an enforcer, since the broker can only withhold the next match, and not the bank's letter of credit, where nobody trusts anyone and each party transacts with the bank.

items.item: Enemy at both doors: a third party whose harm falls on both makes defection between them costlier than cooperation, as two shipping lines form a conference against a third, two restaurants co-fund a street festival against the mall, two firms share one lawyer against a regulator; the carrier is an adversary that exploits any gap between the pair, the first move is safe because the enemy punishes non-cooperation more than the partner could, and the residue is that the cooperation is indexed to the enemy, has no floor when the enemy is gone, and each partner has taught the other how it fights; one side can counterfeit this by inventing the enemy, and then the ignition carries the probe's residue.
items.why: The closing clause, that one side can counterfeit this by inventing the enemy, is already an item in two grown lists (cooperative-masks' manufactured shared enemy, impasse-inventions' commissioned common enemy) and the brief requires the item to say what it adds. It adds two residues the other lists lack: an honest enemy leaves an alliance with no floor once it is gone, and a staged one leaves the stager a secret to keep. Said so.
items.repair: Enemy at both doors: a third party whose harm falls on both makes defection between them costlier than cooperation, as two shipping lines form a conference against a third, two restaurants co-fund a street festival against the mall, two firms share one lawyer against a regulator; the carrier is an adversary that exploits any gap between the pair, the first move is safe because the enemy punishes non-cooperation more than the partner could, and the residue is that the cooperation is indexed to the enemy, has no floor when the enemy is gone, and each partner has taught the other how it fights; one side can counterfeit this by inventing the enemy, which cooperative-masks names as the manufactured shared enemy and impasse-inventions as the commissioned one, and what this item adds is the residue on each side of the counterfeit: an honest enemy leaves an alliance with no floor, and a staged one leaves the stager the probe's secret to keep and an enemy that must go on being fed.

items.item: Same cell: two parties are placed together with no exit by a third who did not consult them, as cellmates assigned, conscripts bunked, co-founders who signed one lease, two firms condemned to share one pier; the carrier is an imposed future in which the other cannot disappear, the first move is safe because the shadow of the future is already there without anyone's choosing it, and the residue is that the cooperation is an artifact of the cage and ends at release, since neither party ever chose the other and neither has learned whether it would; not the wall, which is a task, and not the enemy, which has a face; the cage is exit removed and nothing else.
items.why: The mechanism is 'placed together by a third who did not consult them', and co-founders who signed one lease chose each other and signed by choice; that case is a Sin in common or a First cut, not a cage. The other three cases carry the item. Replaced the case with one the mechanism actually fits.
items.repair: Same cell: two parties are placed together with no exit by a third who did not consult them, as cellmates assigned, conscripts bunked, two firms condemned to share one pier, two shops the landlord assigned to one loading dock; the carrier is an imposed future in which the other cannot disappear, the first move is safe because the shadow of the future is already there without anyone's choosing it, and the residue is that the cooperation is an artifact of the cage and ends at release, since neither party ever chose the other and neither has learned whether it would; not the wall, which is a task, and not the enemy, which has a face; the cage is exit removed and nothing else.

items.item: Lot you can lose: the good is cut to a piece small enough that losing it falls below the threshold of grievance, as a freight broker gives a new carrier one load, a restaurant orders one case, a magazine buys one story; the carrier is divisibility, the first move is safe because the worst case is a write-off and not a wound, and the residue is a ladder, since the cooperation can grow only one rung per successful lot and the trial price, set as a loss-leader, must rise later and reads as betrayal when it does; adjacent to cooperation-mechanisms' sequential milestones, which need an agreed plan, this needs none, and what the lot proves is only the lot, which is why salted mines work.
items.why: Tested against Twenty in the till (below) and against Gift already eaten: the restaurant that orders one case chose it and heard a price, the one that finds a case at the back door did neither, and the residues (a ladder, an unpriced debt) let the operator do different things next. Both separate.

items.item: Price after the crop: neither party pays until the thing exists, so the price is a share of an output not yet made, as a landlord and a tenant with no history split the harvest, a lawyer takes a stranger's case for a third of the award, an author signs for a royalty; the carrier is the future output itself, the first move is safe because nothing changes hands now and each side risks only its own labor, and the residue is that every input is disputed, since each party bears the whole cost of what it adds and gets half the yield, so the yardstick becomes the second war; not the wager, which needs the parties to disagree, since this works when they agree and simply have no cash and no trust.
items.why: The mechanism holds and its discriminator against the wager is exact. It is misplaced on the itinerary, not defective; see seriation.

neighbor_test.left: Twenty in the till: one party stages a windfall the other could keep without being caught, as a bar owner leaves a loose twenty in the drawer on a new bartender's first shift or a jeweler overpays a courier by one stone; the carrier is an apparent error, the first move is safe because the stake is small and its return is uncoerced information, and the residue is that the probe must stay secret forever, since a cooperation later found to have begun as a test reads as contempt; not a gift, which announces itself and makes a debt rather than a reading.
neighbor_test.right: Lot you can lose: the good is cut to a piece small enough that losing it falls below the threshold of grievance, as a freight broker gives a new carrier one load, a restaurant orders one case, a magazine buys one story; the carrier is divisibility, the first move is safe because the worst case is a write-off and not a wound, and the residue is a ladder, since the cooperation can grow only one rung per successful lot and the trial price, set as a loss-leader, must rise later and reads as betrayal when it does; adjacent to cooperation-mechanisms' sequential milestones, which need an agreed plan, this needs none, and what the lot proves is only the lot, which is why salted mines work.
neighbor_test.separating_case: The map's engine rests on these two being different, since the whole far end of the itinerary is said to drop to the twenty when staged, so I tried to collapse them: a planted twenty is a lot the counterpart does not know it was given. Case: a freight broker gives a new carrier one load, or the same broker 'mistakenly' overpays that carrier's invoice by two hundred dollars and watches. On the load, the carrier knows it is on trial and performs; what the broker learns is what the carrier does when watched, and the residue is a ladder whose trial rate must later rise. On the overpayment, the carrier does not know a test exists; what comes back is unperformed conduct, and the residue is a secret. They separate on what the mover can read (performed versus unperformed type) and on what it can do next (climb a rung versus never mention it). They do not collapse.

boundary_case: Cash on the barrelhead at a flea market: two strangers, no history, no enforcer, a good and money crossing a table at once. It is tempting because it looks like the purest ignition of all and matches Beach with no faces step for step, since neither party ever holds both goods and either can walk until the hand closes. Ruling: it is not a separate member, and it is not a member of the Beach as written either, since it has faces and therefore a channel: the buyer can complain, the seller can say 'come back Saturday', and the cooperation can grow past spot exchange. What it exposes is that the Beach's survivability comes from the retractable protocol while its residue comes from the missing faces, two different things the item had fused; the repaired Beach says so. The honest nonmember I also tried, an unwitnessed handshake promise between strangers, is out cleanly: it changes nothing about the survivability of the first move, so it is speech, not a mechanism, and Summoned witness is what it becomes the moment an audience is added.

seriation.note: The axis has real endpoints (one hand on the match and the other party never sees it; no hand at all, only a shut door) and the hinge Summoned witness → Beach with no faces teaches something a ranking would not: making breach expensive and making breach impossible are opposite cures, and the beach pays for needing no audience with having no channel. One placement is wrong. Price after the crop sits in the group 'one party lights and aims at a named counterpart' beside gift, hostage, cut, and lot, but in every one of those the mover's exposure precedes the other's assent, while in a sharecrop, a contingency fee, or a royalty nothing is exposed until both have committed; the author's own breath-two gap files it among the ignitions that 'abolish the first move'. It belongs in the both-hands group next to Wager that needs a partner, which is the item its own discriminator is written against, and the walk then reads Rule → Witness → Beach → Crop → Wager → Sin → Promise, where Beach → Crop teaches that deferring the price and removing the faces are two ways of having no first move. The edges use item identities, so the move costs nothing. The far adjacency Enemy → Same cell (the enemy is a cage with a face) holds and is the itinerary's best line.

edges.why: The antecedent is real and can fail, but 'the first move must instead be a thing handed over' overclaims: a wedding or a merger that cannot be cut into lots can also be witnessed, wagered, or shared, and the very next edge says so. The fork is on what exists to be given now, and the label should say that rather than name a single survivor.
edges.repair_label: If the good cannot be cut into a lot small enough to lose, as a bridge, a merger, or a wedding cannot, the ladder is unavailable, and where a thing already made can be handed over the ignition passes to a hostage; the fork at divisibility is on what the other can be given now, not on which single ignition remains.

edges.why: The exclusivity claim is false. A merger, the author's own example of a good that cannot be cut, is routinely closed with an escrow holdback (a hostage for what is already made) and an earn-out (a share of what is not) in the same document; a book contract carries an advance held against delivery and a royalty. The fork survives, the exclusivity does not, and the fork is sharper without it.
edges.repair_label: If the good cannot be cut but can be waited for, the same fork sends the ignition to a share, trading the risk of a small loss now for a dispute over inputs later; the branches are not exclusive, since a merger with an escrow holdback and an earn-out takes both at once, a hostage for what is already made and a share for what is not, so the fork is on what exists to be given and a good half made takes both.

edges.why: The label says a staged enemy makes 'the ignition the probe's', and that conflates two mechanisms that share only a residue. The twenty seeks a reading and then cooperates honestly on what it read; the staged enemy seeks the cooperation itself and reads nothing. They share the residue exactly (secrecy, and discovery that re-reads the whole cooperation as manipulation), which is the passage's real content and is the author's marked inference. Saying 'not a probe, but the probe's residue' keeps the passage and stops it from domesticating a manipulation into a test. The 'Can recruit' clause survives untouched.
edges.repair_label: If the enemy at both doors was staged by one of them, the ignition is not a probe, since it seeks the cooperation and not a reading, but it inherits the probe's residue exactly: the staging must stay secret, and its discovery converts the whole cooperation into evidence of manipulation; what it adds to the twenty's residue is that a counterfeit circumstance keeps costing, since the enemy must go on being fed. Can recruit: any circumstance at the far end of the itinerary, since a cargo can be arranged to rot, a wall can be built, and a cell can be chosen.

edges.why: The label is a real conditional (if no claim ever comes, the pool is never tested and the edge never fires) and the two-ignition claim teaches. But form_inference calls this a loop, and one back-edge is not a loop; nothing returns from the lot to the pool. It is a re-ignition, a passage from a promise to a lot at the first claim. The edge stays; the form claim should be renamed.

A real incompatibility with a failable antecedent (the secret's statute can expire, or the forbidden thing can be legalized, and then a witness can be summoned). A bare sequence would have shown nothing here, since the two sit five places apart.

A genuine passage between levels with a failable antecedent (a fair that does not recur leaves no record-keeper). The toll-to-cut line is the map's most usable inference for anyone who runs a recurring event.

modality_problems: 'Schelling's asymmetry' (Hostage before the ask): the condition that a hostage be precious to the giver and worth little to the holder is Williamson's ugly-princess argument in 'Credible Commitments' (1983); Schelling discussed hostages as commitment devices without that asymmetry. Repaired in the item.

Source escrow and the unrequested bond (Hostage before the ask) are presented as instances of a thing the counterpart can destroy but not use; both are held by a third and give the counterpart use or money on release. Repaired with cases that fit.

'The escrowed darknet sale' (Beach with no faces) is asserted to reproduce a faceless retractable protocol; it runs on a market that holds the money, which is a broker. 'The two-key drop' names nothing findable. Repaired to the atomic swap.
A hull deductible (Wager that needs a partner) is described as two parties splitting a disagreement about a fact; a deductible is a moral-hazard and small-claims device. Repaired.

'Arrives when the promiser is poorest' (Promise that costs nothing yet) is stated as the general residue; it holds only for a common shock. Repaired to the mechanism that holds for all mutuals, that paying buys the payer nothing at the moment of the first claim.

'A rule nobody wrote, the shipping container' (Rule against myself): ISO 668 was written, by a committee, in 1968. 'A rule whose author is gone' is the honest phrase and loses nothing; left in the item as a flourish since the mechanism does not depend on it, but the atlas record should not repeat it as fact.

'Reads as contempt' (Twenty in the till) is the author's psychology, not observed; in trades where honesty shops are customary, discovery reads as routine and the secret residue shrinks, which bounds the Enemy at both doors passage. Kept as marked inference; noted so the passage is not read as universal.

The Christmas truce of 1914 (Peace of the fair) is listed among suspensions 'so strangers can trade'; it was a truce in which some trading happened. Already covered by the third boundary claim; no repair.
The type's 'no enforcer' is not what the map applies; see strongest objection and the replacement of-sentence there.
duplication: No grown list is duplicated as a whole, and the map's per-item triple (carrier, survivability, residue) is not present in any of them. Partial overlaps that the items should acknowledge, and after repair do: Gift already eaten's residue is cooperative-masks' 'favor unasked-for, priced later'; Enemy at both doors' counterfeit clause is cooperative-masks' 'shared enemy manufactured' and impasse-inventions' 'common enemy commissioned'; Wager that needs a partner's earn-out is impasse-inventions' 'graduated tie' and 'contingent clause'; Promise that costs nothing yet is cooperation-mechanisms' 'mutualization of risk through insurance pools' seen at its first instant; Hostage before the ask is adjacent to cooperation-mechanisms' 'mutual vulnerability deliberately exchanged' but is one-way and unasked, which is the point; First cut is cooperation-mechanisms' 'high exit costs from specialized infrastructure' as a first move rather than a steady state, which the item could say but does not need to.
best_unresolved_seed: The customary ignition. Several of these mechanisms have been lit so often in one trade that nobody lights them any more: the trial load is what freight is, the honesty shop is what retail does, the fair recurs until it is a market. Each time an ignition becomes custom it migrates along the itinerary from 'one hand, aimed' to 'nobody lights it', and it sheds its residue as it goes (the twenty stops being a secret, the lot's trial price stops reading as betrayal, the fair's peace becomes the exchange's rulebook). That is a passage the map does not contain: custom as a Rule against myself lit by the whole trade at once, and a second map of which ignitions each trade has institutionalized, what residue institutionalization removed, and which residue it cannot remove (the broker's cut, the wall's end at the repair). The ledger's own next opening, whether a party who suspects staging can test for it without burning the cooperation, is the same seed from the other side, since the cheapest test for staging is to ask whether the circumstance is one the trade lights for everyone.
independent_review_line: Fable critic: admitted after repairing the type's no-enforcer clause to the criterion the author actually applied, removing a false exclusivity from the divisibility fork, relabeling the staged-circumstance passage so a manipulation is not called a probe, and repairing seven items whose illustrative cases or attributions did not carry their own mechanism.
